description: Issue #746 (Sprites half of the alias/Sprites shadowing fix, landed with #742): with `sprites` ACTIVE, redefining one of the profile's three turtle-identity reporters raises `ol-reserved-word`. `spec/tooling.md:184` is a normative Layer-2 "Required behavior" row -- "Redefining a reserved word, **primitive**, existing procedure, existing type constructor, or existing alias -> `ol-reserved-word`" -- and `:175-176` requires it be applied against the active profile set. `new_turtle`/`who`/`turtles` are Sprites **primitives** (`spec/turtles-and-sprites.md`'s "Canonical forms" table: each Kind-R, arity 0), so with the profile claimed they must collide exactly as `grid` (Geometry), `set_tempo` (Sound), `dict` (Data), and `wait` (Interaction & Events) already did; before this fix the Sprites table was simply never consulted and `define who` was silently accepted, leaving a claimed profile with a normative requirement unmet. This fixture used to pin `namespace: "primitive"` to distinguish these reporters from the block-heads `tell`/`ask`/`each`, which the sibling `reserved-procedures-with-sprites` pinned as `reserved`. Issue #838 removed that param: spec/error-model.md:125,132-141 makes keyword-vs-primitive "an implementation distinction the learner never has to learn", so the two categories are still reported by different BRANCHES of the checker and by the same DIAGNOSTIC. Paired with `reserved-reporters-without-sprites`, which checks this exact source under Core+Turtle alone and is clean -- the profile gate #841 will retire. `"check": true` (semantic-checker only, no execution) because this is a checker rule: the procedures are never called and no events are produced.
